query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Laser cladding a coating composed of a CoCrFeMnNi-based high-entropy alloy (HEA) reinforced with tungsten carbide (WC) particles onto TC4 (Ti6Al4V) surfaces will improve surface hardness and wear resistance without degrading the alloy’s inherent beneficial properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Unmodified TC4 (Ti6Al4V) alloy exhibiting a dual-phase α+β microstructure with relatively low surface hardness and poor wear resistance.
generation.intervention: Apply a laser cladded composite coating consisting of a CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA matrix reinforced with an optimized weight percentage (e.g., around 20 wt.%) of WC particles onto the TC4 substrate.
generation.conditions: The coating will be deposited under an inert atmosphere (e.g., argon) using laser cladding. Afterwards, tribological performance will be evaluated at room temperature under moderate loads using a ball-on-disk test setup, consistent with standard TC4 wear testing conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: A dense, metallurgically bonded composite coating forms with a dual-phase structure: a hardened HEA matrix integrated with uniformly dispersed WC particles. The WC particles serve as micro-scale reinforcements that hinder dislocation motion, pin grain boundaries, and block crack and wear particle formation.
generation.mechanism: The combined effects of solid solution strengthening from the HEA matrix, dispersion strengthening via WC particles, and rapid solidification-induced grain refinement enhance hardness. This, in turn, reduces both adhesive and abrasive wear by providing a stable, hard barrier against micro-plastic deformation and crack propagation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to untreated TC4, the coated surface is predicted to show significantly increased surface hardness (potentially at least 1.5–2 times higher) and a markedly lower wear rate, while preserving other favorable features such as corrosion resistance.
generation.baseline: Untreated TC4 alloy with its known lower hardness and higher wear rate under standard service conditions.
generation.boundary: The predicted improvements apply under room temperature and moderate mechanical stress conditions typical of conventional tribological tests; extreme temperatures or loads may impose additional challenges not addressed by this coating.
generation.uncertainty: While the qualitative improvements in hardness and wear resistance are supported by related studies, the exact quantitative enhancement and long-term durability under varied service environments require further experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of TC4 samples: one set receives the laser cladded CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA coating reinforced with 20 wt.% WC particles, and the control set remains untreated. Use identical laser cladding parameters under an inert atmosphere to ensure consistent coating quality. After coating, perform standardized ball-on-disk tribological tests at room temperature under moderate loads and assess microhardness using Vickers testing. Complement these tests with SEM analysis of the coating’s microstructure and the wear track morphology.
measurements: Surface hardness (Vickers HV) of coated versus uncoated samples.
Wear rate (mm³/(N·m)) obtained from the tribological tests.
Coating adhesion and microstructural integrity via SEM/TEM imaging of the worn surfaces.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated TC4 samples do not exhibit at least a 50% improvement in surface hardness and a statistically significant reduction in wear rate compared to uncoated TC4, or if the coating shows premature delamination or microstructural instability during testing, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: In Figure 10g–i, it can be seen that in the wear morphology of the HEA/WC coating, only a small amount of spalling and slight grooves occurred due to the high hardness. Owing to the production of hard compounds in the coating, the wear mechanism was transformed into abrasive wear. Compared with the HEA coating, the HEA/WC coating had better wear resistance and a narrower width of wear marks. As seen in Figure 10j–l, the morphology of the HEA/WC + CeO2 coating was the best after wear, and the wear width was the narrowest. The wear characteristics of the coating were mostly grooves without spalling or cracking. This shows clearly that CeO2 can indeed refine the grain structure, reduce the cracking sensitivity of the coating, improve the wear resistance and toughness of the coating, and extend the service life of the workpiece.

Although the hardness of AlCrFeNiV with a dual-phase BCC structure is very high, its plasticity is poor. When it is worn by the grinding ball with higher hardness, the material surface is prone to fracture, which means the increase in crushing degree, which is often accompanied by the generation of many fragments on the contact interface. They have sharp edges and a secondary grinding effect during sliding, increasing wear rates. In addition, the wear rate of the alloy in deionized water is significantly lower than that in dry conditions, probably due to lubrication.
